Deployment tradeoffs: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
Timeline and next steps for POC
questions: What latency SLOs are realistic on Hosted vs Dedicated for our model mix?
How long does Private on-prem provisioning typically take?
What telemetry and audit logs are available for Dedicated clusters?
Can Redwood support our KMS/HSM integration and customer-managed keys?
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: All right everyone, thanks for joining. we can do intros quick — im Maya, AE for Redwood. Rafael is our SE and Natalie is our CSM.
[00:12] Priya Patel: Hi. Priya here, head of ML at LumenGrid. we've got Marcus infra and Dana our CTO on too.
[00:20] Marcus Lee: morning.
[00:25] Maya Chen: Great. Goal for today — nail down POC success criteria, understand workload and decide which hosting route we should target: Hosted, Dedicated, or Private. will try to keep to 45 minutes but we have time.
[00:37] Dana Owens: Good. Quick context — we're building an assistant that processes customer telemetry and returns summarized remediation steps. sensitive data lives in EMEA and US, and we have some regs about not moving raw telemetry offsite.
[00:51] Rafael Ortiz: Thanks. can you give ballpark qps, average tokens per request, and peak concurrency so we can size the pilot?
[01:05] Priya Patel: Sure. typical request is around 350 tokens on average. baseline is 6 qps steady, peaks at 60 qps during batch windows. daily token volume roughly 3.2M tokens currently, expecting 2x growth in six months.
[01:24] Jorge Alvarez: also note 20% of calls include user PII; we want to ensure encryption and audit logs.
[01:33] Maya Chen: Perfect — that's helpful. so success criteria from Redwood's perspective and what we usually see: latency SLOs (p95) we can target, throughput/steady-state cost, correctness/quality thresholds using a prompt set, and operational controls like SLO alerts and failover.
[01:51] Priya Patel: On latency, we want p95 under 250ms for typical inference (<=512 tokens). is that realistic?
[01:58] Rafael Ortiz: On Hosted API, depending on the model variant, sub-250ms p95 for 512-token-ish responses is aggressive but doable for smaller models; larger models push you up. Dedicated gives more predictable p95 because you control pools and autoscaling. Private on-prem you'll be constrained by your infra but you can tune for it. caveat: network hop and client-side batching affect the p95 number too.
[02:22] Marcus Lee: What's the usual unit cost difference? ballspark hosted vs dedicated?
[02:28] Maya Chen: Roughly, Hosted is higher per-token but no infra ops; Dedicated lowers unit cost with reserved capacity commitments. Private can be lowest variable cost if you amortize GPU infra, but upfront integration time and ops overhead are higher. we'll put numbers in the SOW.
[02:40] Priya Patel: For compliance we need keys never leaving our control. Can Redwood integrate with our AWS KMS or HSM?
[02:48] Natalie Park: yes — for Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) integrations and full audit logs. Hosted supports envelope encryption and we can discuss bring-your-own-key patterns for enterprise. i'll follow up with the security packet.
[03:02] Dana Owens: And do you have SOC2 and ISO docs?
[03:06] Natalie Park: yes — SOC2 type II available, plus standard pen test summaries. i'll attach the pack.
[03:12] Rafael Ortiz: back to sizing — if you're at 3.2M tokens/day now, doubling in six months, we'd run a benchmark sim with a 48-hour trace you provide. plan is: baseline run on Hosted to measure end-to-end latency, then a Dedicated-config run to compare steady-state throughput and cost. if Private is a requirement for data residency, we'll simulate the same workload in a VPC-connected staging environment to capture network effects.
[03:38] Priya Patel: timeline? how long to set up Dedicated cluster for a pilot?
[03:43] Rafael Ortiz: For Dedicated reserved pools we typically provision a pilot pool in 3–7 business days once we confirm sizing and capacity commitments. Private on-prem can take 4–8 weeks depending on networking and procurement. Hosted is immediate — you can start testing within hours.
[03:58] Marcus Lee: We also want to measure KV cache hit rate — our prompts reuse prefixes a lot. how do you instrument that?
[04:05] Rafael Ortiz: our runtime exposes cache telemetry: hit/miss rates, token savings, and CPU/GPU utilization per model. we'll include instrumentation hooks so your engineers can correlate cache hits with cost per inference.
[04:17] Jorge Alvarez: A key question: if we pick Hosted initially and later move to Dedicated, how seamless is the model routing and rollout?
[04:25] Maya Chen: Seamless — same API and model catalog. you can pin model versions and we support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to a compatible hosted variant if Dedicated capacity is constrained.
[04:35] Priya Patel: For the benchmark data, do you need raw telemetry or anonymized traces?
[04:40] Rafael Ortiz: anonymized is fine; we only need request/response size, token counts, timing, error rates, and sample prompts for quality checks.
[04:49] Dana Owens: Okey. cost sensitivity: what's the estimate for 3.2M tokens/day on Hosted?
[04:56] Maya Chen: i'll put precise numbers in the SOW — high level: Hosted is likely 25–40% higher per-token than a comparable Dedicated reservation at that scale, variable on model family and quantization.
[05:08] Marcus Lee: Are there pre-built connectors for our internal auth? we use Okta with SAML, and infra is locked down behind strict egress controls.
[05:16] Natalie Park: SSO via SAML/Okta is supported. for Dedicated and Private we'll work with your infra team to open minimal egress or use private peering. natalie to coordinate.
[05:27] Priya Patel: For quality, we need acceptance criteria. proposal: run 500 seeded prompts and expect >92% pass rate on our rubric (accuracy + hallucination tolerance). we also want latency p95 < 300ms on our staging traffic.
[05:42] Rafael Ortiz: that's a very workable acceptance criteria. we'll run the same prompt set across Hosted and Dedicated runs and produce a comparison table: pass rate, p95, median latency, tokens per second, cost per 1M tokens, and cache hit rate.
[05:57] Maya Chen: any legal/procurement timeline constraints we should know about?
[06:01] Dana Owens: target quarter for production is Q1 next year. procurement needs about 4–6 weeks for enterprise contract review. if the POC starts this month we can be on track.
[06:11] Priya Patel: what about rollback/failure modes? e.g., if Dedicated cluster has issues, how fast can you failover to Hosted?
[06:18] Rafael Ortiz: We can configure automatic fallback policies. in practice failover time is dominated by client DNS and routing, but we can orchestrate connections to move traffic within minutes if necessary. we'll document RTO/RPO in the SOW.
[06:29] Jorge Alvarez: network egress costs are concern for Private — do you have any guidance?
[06:34] Maya Chen: Private means your infra handles egress — Redwood won't bill for egress in that model; for Dedicated we can estimate egress in SOW. Hosted has standard per-token pricing and any cloud egress is absorbed by Redwood in hosted model (we'll detail).
[06:49] Priya Patel: one more: can you support customer-managed model weights for on-prem? we have some internal fine-tuned variants.
[06:57] Rafael Ortiz: yes for Private we can host your weights; Dedicated can host customer model artifacts in isolated storage. Hosted has limitations for custom private weights but we have partner patterns for secure model onboarding. we'll note feasibility in the SOW.
[07:12] Maya Chen: ok to recap and next steps: Redwood sends SOW with two pilot tracks — Hosted quick-run and Dedicated pilot — plus security packet. Customer shares anonymized 48-hour traces and seeded prompt set. SE schedules benchmark run. Decision meeting 9/30 to confirm hosting preference.
[07:29] Priya Patel: sounds good. one ask: please include explicit runbook items for network changes needed for Dedicated and Private.
[07:36] Marcus Lee: and include expected lead times in the doc.
[07:40] Natalie Park: will do. i'll add network checklist and lead times to the packet.
[07:44] Dana Owens: great. thanks everyone.
[07:47] Maya Chen: thanks all — we'll follow up with docs and calendar invites.
[07:52] (call ends)

Notes: occasional transcription noise — names and product terms may be slightly mis-transcribed. Action items recorded above.
